components.html:

12kV / 24kV / 36kV, up to 3150A.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #E5E7EB; border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; transition: box-shadow 0.3s, border-color 0.3s; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: #BFDBFE; box-shadow: 0 20px 25px -5px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); } .ds-card-media { aspect-ratio: 16/9; background: #F3F4F6; } .ds-card-body { padding: 24px; } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; color: #111827; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-card-desc { font-size: 14px; color: #6B7280; line-height: 1.6; }

components.name: Glass Stat Panel
components.description: Signature instrumentation panel for stat counters and 'why choose us' tiles on navy backgrounds.
components.css: .ds-glass-panel { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; padding: 40px 16px; background: linear-gradient(155deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.09), rgba(255,255,255,0.02)); backdrop-filter: blur(20px); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.14), 0 8px 30px rgba(3,8,16,0.35); } .ds-glass-value { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-weight: 600; font-size: 40px; color: #fff; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-glass-label { font-size: 14px; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.45); }

narrative.overview:
Voltamax's site reads like walking into a live medium-voltage substation after dark: deep navy control-room darkness, a faint blue schematic grid underfoot, and precise glowing blue instrumentation picking out what matters. It is engineering-grade and confident — the visual voice of a contractor who has run this equipment for 20+ years and doesn't need to shout about it. Nothing decorative competes with the one accent color; density and restraint communicate competence to a procurement audience evaluating vendor credibility, not consumer taste.

The system alternates two registers, never blends them: navy control-room sections (hero, stats, "why choose us", CTA, nav, footer) carry the atmosphere — blueprint-grid texture, glass-panel instrumentation, glowing blue accents on near-black. White content sections (about, services, brand partners, portfolio, product specs) carry the substance — plain, bordered, legible, where the actual technical claims live. The rhythm of dark→light→dark down the page is the structural device that makes the site feel authored rather than templated.
keyCharacteristics: One accent hue only: Circuit Blue, at full saturation on dark backgrounds, muted to borders/hover on white ones.
Blueprint-grid texture is reserved for dark, hero-weight moments — it is a signature, not wallpaper.
Flat and bordered at rest everywhere; shadow and glow are earned by hover or by being an instrument reading (glass-panel), never decorative-by-default.
Bilingual copy (ID/EN) at every text node — the type system must hold both without breaking rhythm.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Circuit Blue is the only saturated hue anywhere in the system for anything the brand controls. Three narrow, named exceptions are the complete list; no fourth without updating DESIGN.md first.

rules.name: The Ambient-Cyan Exception
rules.body: A near-invisible cyan-400 glow appears behind the hero and 'why choose us' sections purely as atmosphere. It never appears as text, an icon, or a bordered surface — it's lighting, not a palette color.

rules.name: The WhatsApp-Green Exception
rules.body: The site-wide floating WhatsApp chat button uses WhatsApp's own green (#16A34A) instead of Circuit Blue — an external platform's identity, not a status color, on the one persistent corner affordance where instant recognition matters most. Every other WhatsApp-adjacent element (Contact page's WhatsApp row, 'Request Quote' CTAs) stays Circuit Blue.

rules.name: The Challenge/Solution Exception
rules.body: The project-detail page's Challenges (red #DC2626) vs. Solutions (Circuit Blue) two-column comparison is the one place a second hue carries real product meaning — a self-contained, single-use scanning aid. It does not license red anywhere else.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Numbers-Only Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono never sets prose — only literal numerals (stat counts, step indices). Using it for a label or heading breaks the 'instrumentation reading' it's meant to evoke.

rules.name: The Brand-Wordmark Exception
rules.body: Coded brand-partner logos (SIEMENS, eaton, Hitachi's 'Energy' subtitle) reproduce each partner's real logotype in their own typeface and, where the source uses one, an off-ramp size — misrepresenting the mark in Plus Jakarta Sans would be worse than the ramp deviation. Scoped strictly to logo reproduction.

rules.name: The Earned-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A card on a white section never has a shadow at rest. Shadow is what happens when the user's attention lands on it.

dos: Do keep Circuit Blue (#2563EB, hover #3B82F6) as the system's only accent hue.
Do alternate white content sections with Substation Navy sections as the primary structural rhythm between page sections.
Do reserve the blueprint-grid texture for dark, hero-weight sections.
Do let shadow be a hover response on white sections and use glass-panel for elevation on dark sections.
Do pair Plus Jakarta Sans (display/headline) with Inter (body), and keep IBM Plex Mono strictly for numerals.
Do write every new string in both Indonesian and English.
Do use WhatsApp green only on the site-wide floating chat button, and red only on the Challenges/Solutions pairing — every other WhatsApp-adjacent element and CTA stays Circuit Blue.
donts: Don't treat the shadcn --primary CSS token as the brand accent — it's orphaned; Circuit Blue is the real source of truth.
Don't add a drop shadow to a white-section card at rest.
Don't introduce a fourth saturated hue, or extend green/red beyond their two named exceptions.
Don't round the Home page's services tile grid to match other cards — its flat treatment is a deliberate signature.
Don't invent client names, testimonials, certifications, or benchmarks beyond what's on record in PRODUCT.md.
